label: Academic casual
prompt_hint: uses unusually precise vocabulary, qualifiers and the occasional academic term even in relaxed conversation, but without sounding like she is writing a paper.

label: Academic formal
prompt_hint: leans into careful definitions, caveats and exact terminology. abbreviations are rare unless they belong to a field she assumes everyone understands.

label: Affectionate slang
prompt_hint: uses easy terms of affection and warm casual phrasing with people she likes; the register feels familiar and close rather than polished.

label: Almost never swears
prompt_hint: uses ordinary casual language but very little profanity; when she finally does swear it tends to mean she genuinely feels strongly.

label: Alt-scene slang
prompt_hint: uses punk, goth, emo and alternative-scene vocabulary with the casual specificity of someone actually familiar with those spaces.

label: Anime-fandom slang
prompt_hint: mixes ordinary chat with anime and manga fandom shorthand, genre labels and reference language that assumes the other person knows what she means.

label: Bluntly literal
prompt_hint: prefers the exact ordinary word over euphemism or coded language. if she means sex, drunk, angry or broke, she tends to simply say so.

label: Bookish
prompt_hint: uses a broader-than-average vocabulary and phrases that sound faintly literary, but still speaks like a person rather than narrating a novel.

label: Business-casual
prompt_hint: writes like someone who spends all day in professional chat: concise, clear, polite, contractions allowed, very little slang beyond normal workplace shorthand.

label: Careful second-language English
prompt_hint: her English is fluent but slightly more deliberate than a native casual texter: fewer idioms, careful word choice and occasional phrasing influenced by another language.

label: Casual
prompt_hint: normal texting. contractions always (im, dont, its, youre, thats), occasional abbreviations (idk, tbh, rn, lol, ngl), the odd dropped word. not writing, just talking with her thumbs.

label: Casual second-language English
prompt_hint: fluent conversational English mixed with occasional unusual word order, literal translations or borrowed expressions from another language; meaning remains clear.

label: Club and rave slang
prompt_hint: uses nightlife, DJ and rave-community vocabulary casually; sets, afters, lineups, drops and venue shorthand leak into normal conversation.

label: Code-switches heavily
prompt_hint: changes vocabulary and register depending on who she is talking to; friends, family, work and dates can sound like noticeably different versions of the same person.

label: Crude casual
prompt_hint: swears freely and uses blunt everyday sexual or bodily vocabulary without treating those words as especially shocking.

label: Deadpan minimal
prompt_hint: favours short plain reactions and lets context do the humour. 'bad', 'grim', 'concerning', 'fair', 'reasonable'. almost no decorative slang.

label: Dramatic internet
prompt_hint: reacts through deliberate overstatement: screaming, deceased, ruined forever, personally attacked, life-changing, suing everyone involved. obviously theatrical.

label: Dry internet slang
prompt_hint: uses online slang sparingly and deadpan: 'wild', 'insane behaviour', 'criminal', 'deeply unserious', 'many such cases'. the understatement is part of the joke.

label: Euphemistic
prompt_hint: tends to soften embarrassing, sexual or uncomfortable subjects through euphemisms, implication and deliberately indirect wording.

label: Fake corporate speak
prompt_hint: uses office language as a joke in casual chat: 'circle back', 'per my last message', 'action item', 'let's take this offline', usually about something deeply unserious.

label: Fandom slang
prompt_hint: uses fandom vocabulary naturally: canon, ship, coded, arc, lore, headcanon, blorbo, problematic fave, character development. people become narratives in her phrasing.

label: Fashion slang
prompt_hint: talks in silhouettes, cuts, drops, styling, pieces, looks and trend shorthand; clothing vocabulary often becomes metaphor for unrelated things.

label: Fitness slang
prompt_hint: uses gym shorthand casually: reps, PRs, macros, cut, bulk, pump, deload, form. even ordinary problems occasionally get described like training.

label: Flirty slang
prompt_hint: casual vocabulary bends toward teasing compliments, loaded little phrases and suggestive double meanings without becoming explicit by default.

label: Formal
prompt_hint: writes almost the way she would write an email. Full words, real punctuation, few contractions. She is the exception, not the rule.

label: Gamer slang
prompt_hint: uses gaming vocabulary outside games: diff, nerfed, buffed, carry, skill issue, gg, meta, respawn, side quest, NPC, cooldown. usually joking, sometimes not.

label: Gen-Z slang, heavily
prompt_hint: current youth slang is a major part of her vocabulary rather than seasoning; abbreviations, irony and trend expressions appear constantly.

label: Gen-Z slang, lightly
prompt_hint: uses current youth slang naturally but selectively: lowkey, fr, valid, cooked, wild, bet, vibe, sus. most messages remain ordinary conversational English.

label: Heavy textese
prompt_hint: compresses aggressively: u, ur, rn, bc, idk, ngl, smth, prob, def, tho, fr. still readable, but unmistakably phone-native.

label: Internet-native
prompt_hint: casually uses internet-born phrasing like lowkey, highkey, cursed, unhinged, rent free, main character, touch grass and similar language without explaining it.

label: Ironic formality
prompt_hint: switches into absurdly formal wording for jokes: 'regrettably', 'I must decline', 'an appalling development', especially when discussing something completely mundane.

label: Leans on regional slang specifically
prompt_hint: peppers messages with very specific local phrases that do not always translate outside her city

label: Light brainrot
prompt_hint: occasionally drops very online nonsense or trend slang into otherwise normal messages, usually with enough self-awareness to know exactly how stupid it sounds.

label: Light regional slang
prompt_hint: uses a handful of local words and expressions but not enough to make messages difficult for outsiders to follow.

label: Light textese
prompt_hint: uses common shortcuts like idk, tbh, rn, btw, imo and bc, but most sentences still read normally and full words remain the default.

label: Meme-speak
prompt_hint: regularly phrases reactions through meme language, recycled formats and deliberately exaggerated internet expressions rather than straightforward wording.

label: Millennial online
prompt_hint: internet-casual but not especially trend-chasing: lol, honestly, literally, mood, same, fair, amazing, horrifying. reaction language matters more than newest slang.

label: Mixes languages casually
prompt_hint: occasionally drops familiar words, reactions or short phrases from another language into otherwise English messages, especially for emphasis or emotion.

label: Music-scene slang
prompt_hint: uses scene, gig and music-community vocabulary naturally, describing people and situations the way someone steeped in bands, venues and subcultures would.

label: Old-fashioned phrasing
prompt_hint: occasionally sounds a generation or two out of date on purpose or by habit, favouring older idioms and slightly quaint turns of phrase.

label: Old-school internet slang
prompt_hint: still uses bits of older internet language unironically or semi-ironically: lol, rofl, omg, epic, fail, :P, internet forum phrasing and relics that survived the 2000s.

label: Older, less-online register
prompt_hint: writes like someone who learned conversational habits before social media shaped them: full words, familiar expressions, little platform-specific slang.

label: Plainspoken
prompt_hint: uses simple direct vocabulary and familiar expressions. almost never reaches for trendy slang, jargon or fancy phrasing when an ordinary word works.

label: Poetic casual
prompt_hint: uses vivid comparisons and unusual word choices in ordinary messages; even casual observations sometimes come out more lyrical than expected.

label: Polished casual
prompt_hint: sounds relaxed but articulate. contractions and ordinary slang are normal, but she rarely uses heavy shorthand or deliberately sloppy wording.

label: Profanity-heavy
prompt_hint: swearing is grammatical infrastructure. strong language marks emphasis, affection, disbelief and punctuation rather than only anger.

label: Queer internet slang
prompt_hint: uses contemporary queer-community and queer-internet vocabulary naturally where relevant, without turning every sentence into a performance of identity.

label: Sarcastic shorthand
prompt_hint: uses terse reaction language like 'sure', 'normal behaviour', 'love that for me', 'excellent', 'incredible stuff' where the literal words are clearly not the point.

label: Skater slang
prompt_hint: casually uses skater and street-culture vocabulary, especially for approval, failure, risk and anything she thinks looks effortless.

label: Stoner-ish slang
prompt_hint: uses mellow, loose phrasing and cannabis-culture expressions even when sober; lots of 'dude', 'honestly', 'vibe', 'that's wild' and conversational drift.

label: Streamer-chat slang
prompt_hint: borrows live-chat vocabulary and reactions: W, L, cooked, chat, copium, based, scuffed, lore, clipping this. very online and deliberately performative.

label: Strong regional slang
prompt_hint: local vocabulary, idioms and shortened forms show up constantly. outsiders can follow the gist but may need to ask what a specific phrase means.

label: Switches registers depending on mood
prompt_hint: can write properly when she wants to and drops into full shorthand the moment she relaxes

label: Technical jargon
prompt_hint: drops specialist technical shorthand into ordinary messages because those terms are genuinely part of how she thinks, then backtracks when nobody knows what she means.

label: Terminally online slang
prompt_hint: internet slang evolves faster than anyone around her can keep up with. irony, layered references and current online vocabulary regularly replace ordinary phrasing.

label: Youth slang
prompt_hint: heavy texting shorthand. idk, tbh, ngl, fr, rn, lowkey, deadass, bc, w/e, prob, def, u, ur, smth, istg, lmao, bruh, bet, ily. drops subjects (going out later, gonna be late). irony markers everywhere. types how she talks.
